question: What is the height of the geostationary orbit?
solution:
The correct answer is __**35,786 km**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The height of the geostationary orbit is **35,786 km** above Earth's equator.
 
• A geostationary orbit is a circular orbit directly above the Earth's equator, allowing satellites to match the Earth's rotation.
 
• Satellites in this orbit appear stationary relative to an observer on the ground, making them ideal for telecommunications, weather monitoring, and broadcasting.
 
• Geostationary orbits are also known as geosynchronous equatorial orbits (GEO).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of a geostationary satellite was first proposed by the science fiction writer **Arthur C. Clarke** in 1945.
 
• Geostationary satellites are an essential part of global communication networks, allowing for consistent satellite coverage over specific areas.
 
• Maintaining a geostationary orbit requires precise calculations to counteract the gravitational pull of the Earth and other celestial bodies.
 
• The first geostationary satellite, **SYNCOM 3**, was launched by NASA in 1964.
